mainTopic: The end of מסכת גיטין: when divorce is a מצוה, and why divorcing a first wife is so painful
overview: This amud closes מסכת גיטין. It first finishes a ברייתא about a husband who ignores his wife's immodest behavior. The גמרא corrects one phrase: she cannot literally bathe 'with men,' so it means she bathes in a place where men bathe. The ברייתא rules that divorcing such a wife is a מצוה מן התורה. It reads 'another man' (איש אחר) as a judgment on the next husband: he brought in the wicked woman the first husband sent away. So the next husband either merits to divorce her or deserves to die. The גמרא then quotes 'כי שנא שלח' from מלאכי. רבי יהודה reads it as 'if you hate her, divorce her,' and רבי יוחנן reads it as 'the one who divorces is hated.' The גמרא says they do not argue: one speaks of a first marriage and the other of a second. רבי אלעזר proves that a first marriage is special: when a man divorces his first wife, even the מזבח sheds tears. The מסכת ends with the הדרן.

steps.title: The last details of the immodest wife
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes listing the immodest behavior that a bad husband ignores. She wears a garment open on both sides and bathes 'with men.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And she goes about with her garment open on both sides, and bathes with men.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its description of a wife who acts immodestly while her husband does nothing about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are the last items in a list that began before this section. The phrase 'bathes with men' will be questioned in the very next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Torn open, with her garment split

phrases.english: and with her garment open on both sides,
and bathing with men.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפְרוּמָה מִשְּׁנֵי צְדָדֶיהָ, וְרוֹחֶצֶת עִם בְּנֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The worst kind of husband lets his wife go about immodestly dressed and bathe 'with men.'

steps.title: Could she really bathe with men?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to the plain meaning of 'bathing with men.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'With men'? Could you really think that?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops and asks whether the ברייתא can really mean that she bathes together with men.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read literally, the phrase describes something so extreme that even the worst husband would not allow it. The גמרא is setting up a corrected reading in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? Used to say something cannot be meant literally

phrases.english: 'With men'? Could that enter your mind?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא in step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'רוחצת עם בני אדם' in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No husband, however bad, would allow his wife to bathe together with men, so the literal reading cannot be right.

steps.title: It means a place where men bathe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reinterprets the phrase: she bathes in a place where men usually bathe.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means she bathes in a place where men bathe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. She does not bathe with men; she bathes in a spot where men commonly bathe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This keeps the ברייתא's point, that she acts without modesty, while removing the impossible literal meaning. Bathing where men often come is still immodest behavior that the husband should not ignore.

phrases.english: Rather, in a place where men bathe.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: She literally bathes together with men.
steps.terutzMaskana: She bathes in a place where men usually bathe.

steps.title: A Torah מצוה to divorce her
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that it is a מצוה מן התורה to divorce this kind of wife, and brings a פסוק as its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: This woman: it is a מצוה from the Torah to divorce her, as it says: 'For he found in her something unseemly... and he sends her out of his house.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the ruling. A husband whose wife behaves this way has a Torah מצוה to divorce her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source is the פסוק about a man who 'found in her ערות דבר' and 'sends her from his house.' Immodest behavior counts as that kind of unseemly matter, so divorce here is a מצוה, not just permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc. The rest of the פסוק

phrases.english: This one: it is a מצוה from the Torah to divorce her,
as it is stated: 'Because he found in her an unseemly [matter], etc.'
'and he sends her out of his house.'

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹ – מִצְוָה מִן הַתּוֹרָה לְגָרְשָׁהּ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא after the side clarification and gives its ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is a מצוה מן התורה to divorce a wife who behaves immodestly, based on 'כי מצא בה ערות דבר... ושלחה מביתו.'

steps.title: Why the next husband is called 'another'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא reads the word 'another' (אחר) in the next פסוק as a sign that the second husband is morally unlike the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And she goes and becomes another man's wife.' The פסוק calls him 'other' to teach that he is no match for the first husband. The first removed a wicked woman from his house, and this one brought a wicked woman into his house.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains why the Torah calls the second husband 'another man.' It is a judgment of his character.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אחר seems extra, since obviously a second husband is someone else. So the ברייתא reads it as saying he is 'different' from the first: the first did right by sending away a wicked wife, while the second did wrong by taking her in.

keyTerms.meaning: Other, another. Read here as 'different in character'

phrases.english: 'And she goes and becomes another man's [wife]':
the verse called him 'other,'

phrases.aramaic: לוֹמַר: שֶׁאֵין זֶה בֶּן זוּגוֹ לָרִאשׁוֹן –
phrases.english: to say that this one is not the equal of the first:
that one removed a wicked woman from his house,
and this one brought a wicked woman into his house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues into the next פסוק and draws a lesson from its wording
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The second husband is called 'אחר' because he is not on the first husband's level: the first sent a wicked woman out, and the second brought her in.

steps.title: If the second husband merits, he divorces her
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says that if the second husband is worthy, he will end up divorcing her, as the next פסוק describes.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the second husband merits, he sends her away, as it says: 'And the latter man hates her.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא describes the good outcome for the second husband: he merits to come to dislike her and divorce her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists two ways the second marriage can end: the husband hates her and divorces her, or he dies. The ברייתא reads the first option as the reward of a man who 'merits.'

phrases.english: If the second merits, he sends her away,
as it is stated: 'And the latter man hates her.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the reading of the פסוקים about the second husband
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A worthy second husband will come to divorce her, as in 'ושנאה האיש האחרון.'

steps.title: If not, she buries him
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes that if the second husband does not merit, he dies and she buries him. He deserves death for bringing a wicked woman into his home.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if not, she buries him, as it says: 'Or if the latter man dies.' He deserves death, because the first removed a wicked woman from his house, and this one brought a wicked woman into his house.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the bad outcome: if the second husband does not merit, he dies, and he deserves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second option in the פסוק, 'or if the latter man dies,' is read as a punishment. The reason repeats the contrast from step 5: one husband sent wickedness out of his home, and the other invited it in.
steps.whatToRemember: A wife who behaves immodestly should be divorced, as a מצוה מן התורה. The man who then marries her is called 'אחר' because he brought wickedness into his home, so he either merits to divorce her or deserves to die.

phrases.english: And if not, she buries him,
as it is stated: 'Or if the latter man dies':
he deserves death,
because that one removed a wicked woman from his house,
and this one brought a wicked woman into his house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other outcome from the same פסוק as step 6 and closes the ברייתא
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The second husband who marries a wicked divorced woman either merits to divorce her or deserves death, because he brought into his home the wickedness that the first husband removed.

steps.title: Two readings of 'For I hate sending away'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה reads the פסוק as telling a man to divorce a wife he hates. רבי יוחנן reads it as saying that the one who divorces is hated by ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'כי שנא שלח'. רבי יהודה says it means: if you hate her, send her away. רבי יוחנן says it means: the one who sends his wife away is hated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק from מלאכי and shows two opposite ways that רבי יהודה and רבי יוחנן read it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same Hebrew words can be read two ways. רבי יהודה reads 'שנא' as 'if you hate' and 'שלח' as a command: 'send her away.' רבי יוחנן reads it as a description: 'the one who sends away is hated.' On the surface, one reading allows or even encourages divorce, while the other condemns it.

keyTerms.meaning: The words in מלאכי that both opinions are reading
The one who sends away, meaning the one who divorces

phrases.english: "For I hate sending away"
Rabbi Yehuda says:
If you hate her, send her away.
Rabbi Yochanan says:
The one who sends away is hated.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי שָׂנֵא שַׁלַּח רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of the previous steps, which is when divorce is proper, by bringing a new פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: if you hate your wife, divorce her. רבי יוחנן: one who divorces is hated.

steps.title: No real dispute: first marriage versus second marriage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the two opinions do not argue. Each one is talking about a different kind of marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not argue. One statement is about a first marriage, and the other is about a second marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the apparent argument between רבי יהודה and רבי יוחנן by assigning each opinion to a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of leaving two opposite readings in place, the גמרא says each is correct in its own situation. In a first marriage, divorce is hated, which fits רבי יוחנן. In a second marriage, if the husband hates his wife, he may divorce her, which fits רבי יהודה. The next step brings the source for treating a first marriage as special.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not say here which opinion goes with which marriage. The proof in the next step, about the first wife, shows that רבי יוחנן's 'hated' fits the first marriage.

phrases.english: And they do not disagree:
this one is about a first marriage,
and that one is about a second marriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the apparent contradiction between the two readings given in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each opinion applies to a different marriage.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה and רבי יוחנן seem to hold opposite views about divorce.
steps.terutzMaskana: Divorcing a first wife is hated. A second marriage with hatred may be ended.

steps.title: The altar cries over one who divorces his first wife
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that even the מזבח sheds tears over someone who divorces his first wife. He proves it from a פסוק in מלאכי about the 'wife of your youth.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: anyone who divorces his first wife, even the altar sheds tears over him. The נביא says you cover ה׳'s altar with tears, and ה׳ no longer accepts your offerings, because ה׳ is witness between you and the wife of your youth, whom you betrayed, though she is your companion and the wife of your covenant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי אלעזר's teaching as proof that a first marriage has special standing, so divorcing a first wife is hated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of 'the wife of your youth,' which means a first wife. It describes the altar covered in tears and ה׳ refusing offerings because of the betrayal. This supports the split in step 9: a first marriage is a covenant that ה׳ witnessed, so ending it is condemned.

keyTerms.meaning: The altar sheds tears over him

steps.whatToRemember: Divorcing a first wife is so serious that the מזבח cries over it. A first marriage is a covenant that ה׳ witnessed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the closing message of מסכת גיטין. After a whole מסכת about how a גט works, it ends by stressing how painful divorce is, especially from one's first wife.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Elazar said:
Anyone who divorces his first wife,
even the altar sheds tears over him,
as it is stated:
"And this second thing you do:
covering the altar of ה׳ with tears,
with weeping and sighing,
so that He no longer turns to the offering,
nor accepts it willingly from your hand.
And you say: For what reason?
Because ה׳ has been a witness
between you and the wife of your youth,
phrases.notes: 'The wife of your youth' is the key words. It shows the פסוק is talking about a first wife.

phrases.english: whom you have betrayed,
though she is your companion and the wife of your covenant."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the claim in step 9 that a first marriage is different and divorcing a first wife is hated.
steps.raayaObject: That divorcing a first wife is hated, which is the case where רבי יוחנן's reading applies.
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלאכי ב:יג-יד, as taught by רבי אלעזר

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק המגרש and מסכת גיטין
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for פרק המגרש, together with the statement that מסכת גיטין is complete.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק המגרש, and מסכת גיטין is finished.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional closing line said at the end of a פרק. Here it also marks the end of the whole מסכת גיטין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is not part of the argument. It is a farewell to the פרק, a promise to come back and learn it again. Since this is the last פרק, it also announces that the whole מסכת is done.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you, the closing formula at the end of a פרק

steps.whatToRemember: מסכת גיטין ends with the reminder that divorcing a first wife makes even the מזבח cry.

phrases.english: We will return to you, "HaMegaresh"
phrases.notes: 'המגרש' is the name of this last פרק, taken from its first word.

phrases.english: and Tractate Gittin is completed

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק and the מסכת after the final teaching in step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The end of פרק המגרש and of מסכת גיטין.
